briefs.title: Keep the speaker in frame
briefs.description: A focused interview answer with measured face following and word-timed captions.
briefs.promptSource: Original Video Use short-form editing brief; source footage retains its credited license.
briefs.license: MIT for original editing code and documentation; source media retains its own credited terms
briefs.prompt: Use Video Use to turn a useful answer from a filmed interview into a 22-second social clip. Choose one complete thought that answers a clear question. Put the question on screen immediately as an editorial hook, then let the original speaker deliver the answer with no long intro or generic end card. Follow the visible face with measured tracking and a deliberately reviewed target; use a calm crop, never a jittery zoom on every word. Keep the whole head and natural gesture room. Burn accurate phrase captions after all cuts and framing, with at most two lines and one restrained highlighted key word at a time. Preserve small hesitations when they carry meaning; never splice words into a new claim. Use clean speech with short boundary fades; no music under this example. Keep a quiet attribution footer and let the last thought land. Use the real footage supplied in this chat or acquired from the supplied source URL with yt-dlp. Inspect the actual pixels and audio evidence, not only metadata. Keep the subject and intent of the current query. Deliver a polished 1080×1920 vertical MP4 with a readable first-second hook and a clear payoff. Keep important content away from the top 150px, bottom 300px, and rightmost 120px used by social app controls. Use few words, deliberate typography, clean cuts and intentional sound. Preserve meaning, source credits and honest framing; do not invent actions, reactions, quotes or claims. Give me a short preview for approval before completing the full edit in normal interactive use. Keep the editable cut map, source URLs, caption timing, licenses and complete replay instructions.
